summary: Frontend-only retest of iteration_97's CRITICAL stuck-scroll-lock bug, now fixed via the new watchdog/heartbeat design (450ms self-expiring timeout in app/(tabs)/index.tsx, replacing the ref-counter entirely). RESULT: MIXED. The specific bug this fix targeted (permanent stuck-lock after a quick tap) IS FIXED: ran 5 consecutive quick tap (down+up, no drag) cycles on radar-map - each time overflowY correctly went 'hidden' on touch-down and self-released to 'auto' within 600ms after release, 5/5 pass, and page scroll (mouse wheel) worked afterward (scrollTop advanced to 300). HOWEVER, found a NEW CRITICAL issue on the second required test case (a longer 1-2s continuous single-finger drag before release): the lock correctly engages at ~100-200ms into the drag (overflow='hidden'), but then PREMATURELY releases to 'auto' at ~300ms into the drag WHILE THE MOUSE IS STILL DOWN AND ACTIVELY MOVING, and never re-locks for the remaining ~1.2s of the drag despite continuous simulated movement events every 100ms. This directly violates the requirement 'confirm the ScrollView stays locked for the FULL duration of the drag (does not prematurely unlock mid-drag)'. Reproduced consistently in a clean re-run with proper continuous small-increment movement (ruled out a test-script bug from an earlier attempt with a zero-movement first step). Regression checks: zoom +/- buttons and recentre correctly step the Focus Map tier (4->9->16->9->4 sequence verified via focus-summary testID text), Radius/Events sheets open correctly. Double-tap-to-zoom via mouse dblclick did not change the zoom tier in this run (stayed at 'best 4' both times) - inconclusive, likely a web dblclick-timing/target artifact rather than a real regression given zoom buttons work fine, but flagging since review request explicitly asked to re-verify it. No console errors/crashes observed.

integration_issues.flow: Radar touch-interaction watchdog lock (onRadarInteractionStart/onRadarInteractionEnd in app/(tabs)/index.tsx, pinged from RadarView's pan.onTouchesDown + pinch/pan onUpdate)
integration_issues.issue: NEW CRITICAL (different from iter_96/97, but same root symptom class): during a continued single-finger drag with the mouse/finger still down and actively moving, the ScrollView interaction-lock prematurely releases ~300ms into the gesture and never re-engages for the rest of that drag (tested up to 1.5s), even though pan.onUpdate is supposed to re-ping onInteractionStart on every frame of an active drag. Quick taps (no drag) are correctly protected and self-heal (5/5 pass), so the watchdog itself works when it's given at least one refresh signal - the failure is specific to sustained drags, suggesting either (a) pan.onUpdate's continuous re-ping is not actually firing repeatedly on this platform/environment once the gesture is past its initial recognition, or (b) the DOM/style change caused by scrollEnabled flipping true mid-gesture interrupts pointer capture on the Pan gesture handler (web/RNGH), so no further mousemove/touchmove events reach onUpdate at all after the first unlock, creating an unrecoverable one-way trip for the remainder of that gesture. Net effect: a sufficiently long pinch/pan (the exact use case this whole 3-iteration fix chain was protecting) can have the surrounding ScrollView/RefreshControl silently re-enabled mid-gesture, which is the same class of danger (native scroll potentially interrupting/stealing an in-progress pinch and resetting zoom) that iteration_96 originally set out to prevent.

action_items: PASS: retest confirms the specific iteration_97 bug (permanent stuck-lock, onTouchesUp never firing on tap release) is fixed by the 450ms watchdog design - 5/5 quick tap-release cycles recovered correctly and page scroll/pull-to-refresh became usable again after each.

STILL BROKEN (new symptom): a sustained drag (1-2s, mouse continuously down and moving) loses its lock ~300ms in and never regains it for the rest of that gesture, in this web-preview environment. Recommend instrumenting pinch.onUpdate/pan.onUpdate with a temporary counter (e.g. runOnJS a JS counter increment on every onUpdate call) to confirm whether onUpdate is actually still firing after the first unlock, or whether the pointer/gesture is being silently cancelled once scrollEnabled flips true mid-drag (i.e., check if onTouchesCancelled or a gesture state change happens right around the 300ms mark).

If onUpdate IS still firing but the JS state update (setRadarInteracting(true) via runOnJS) simply isn't being applied/re-rendered in time, consider whether React state-update batching/frequency (called every single animation frame, ~60-120/sec) is causing dropped or coalesced setState calls that lose the timer-reset race against the 450ms setTimeout - e.g. clearTimeout+setTimeout inside a state setter called at high frequency could itself be a perf/timing hazard. A ref-based timestamp check (rather than repeatedly clearing/creating setTimeout objects every frame) might be more robust.

Given this is the 3rd fix attempt and the failure mode changed each time (double-count -> onTouchesUp unreliable -> mid-drag premature release), strongly recommend validating on a real iOS/Android device or Expo Go build before further web-preview-only iteration, per the original agent-to-agent note - there may be a fundamental gap between RNGH's web touch/pointer emulation and native touch lifecycle that keeps resurfacing as different symptoms of the same underlying platform gap.
critical_code_review_comments: The heartbeat design (re-ping onInteractionStart every onUpdate frame) is correct in principle but was not verified to actually keep pinging past the initial gesture recognition in this environment - the test evidence (lock drops ~300ms into a still-continuing drag and never recovers) suggests either the re-ping stops firing or the resulting state update stops taking effect once the ScrollView's scrollEnabled/overflow changes mid-gesture, which was not covered by any automated test before this fix was considered complete.

No defensive check exists for 'lock released while a gesture is still logically active' - e.g. tracking a JS-side isDragging boolean set by onTouchesDown/cleared by onTouchesUp/Cancelled, independent of the watchdog, so a mismatch (watchdog says released but native gesture says still active) could at least be logged/detected.

success_rate.frontend: 80% - stuck-lock-on-tap bug from iter_97 is fixed (5/5); zoom buttons/recentre/radius/events sheets pass; NEW critical mid-drag premature-unlock issue found on the long-drag test case

seed_data_creation: None - used existing kauri@intro.demo demo account via 'Explore Demo' (login-demo) button on /login
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login: go to /login, click [data-testid=login-demo], then [data-testid=tab-radar]. Dismiss ping popups via get_by_text('Dismiss', exact=True) in a retry loop (they cover the radar-map and will silently eat mouse events otherwise - this caused a false negative in my first test attempt this round). Scroll container found by walking up parentElement chain from [data-testid=radar-map] until getComputedStyle().overflowY is hidden/auto/scroll (first ancestor is typically 'hidden' when locked, 'auto' when unlocked). For the tap test: mouse.down(), wait ~80ms, check overflow (expect hidden), mouse.up(), wait 600ms, check overflow (expect auto) - 5/5 passed. For the drag test: mouse.down() then IMMEDIATELY start small continuous mouse.move() increments every ~100ms (do NOT insert any stationary hold before the first move - that changes the test and can cause a false premature-unlock reading unrelated to the real bug) for 1.5s while checking overflow each step - found overflow drops to 'auto' at ~300ms and stays that way for the remainder of the drag despite continued movement, which is the real, reproducible bug.
rca_of_issue: The watchdog/heartbeat mechanism correctly protects a single momentary touch (tap) since onTouchesDown alone is enough to arm the 450ms timer and no further refresh is needed before release. But for a sustained drag, the design depends on pinch.onUpdate/pan.onUpdate continuously re-arming that timer every frame; test evidence shows the lock is lost about 300ms into an ongoing drag and never recovers for the rest of that same continuous gesture (mouse never released, movement continues for another ~1.2s), meaning either (a) onUpdate's runOnJS(onInteractionStart) call stops having an effect after the first unlock - possibly because the resulting scrollEnabled/overflow DOM change interrupts pointer capture on the underlying gesture recognizer in this RNGH-web environment, silently ending the gesture's ability to keep firing onUpdate, or (b) the repeated clearTimeout/setTimeout pattern invoked at high frequency inside a React state setter has a timing/batching issue that drops the refresh. Either way, this reintroduces the original risk (native scroll can now start mid-pinch/pan) that all three fix iterations have been trying to eliminate, just in a narrower, less obvious window (mid-drag rather than post-release).
